title: Highland Associates Inc. Invests $14.99 Million in Apple Inc. (AAPL)
text:
Tweet
Highland Associates Inc. bought a new stake in Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) during the 3rd quarter, according to its most recent Form 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The institutional investor bought 66,386 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock, valued at approximately $14,986,000. Apple accounts for about 2.3% of Highland Associates Inc.’s portfolio, making the stock its 8th largest position.
Other hedge funds and other institutional investors have also recently added to or reduced their stakes in the company. Daiwa SB Investments Ltd. boosted its position in Apple by 3.4% during the 2nd quarter. Daiwa SB Investments Ltd. now owns 27,620 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,113,000 after acquiring an additional 900 shares during the last quarter. Augustine Asset Management Inc. boosted its position in Apple by 1.5% during the 2nd quarter. Augustine Asset Management Inc. now owns 63,812 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $11,812,000 after acquiring an additional 963 shares during the last quarter. CX Institutional acquired a new position in Apple during the 2nd quarter worth approximately $135,000. Confluence Investment Management LLC acquired a new position in Apple during the 2nd quarter worth approximately $375,000. Finally, Addenda Capital Inc. boosted its position in Apple by 91.5% during the 2nd quarter. Addenda Capital Inc. now owns 155,634 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $27,400,000 after acquiring an additional 74,349 shares during the last quarter. 57.02% of the stock is currently owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors. AAPL opened at $156.30 on Tuesday. Apple Inc. has a 1-year low of $142.00 and a 1-year high of $233.47. The company has a current ratio of 1.12, a quick ratio of 1.09 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87. The firm has a market capitalization of $775.41 billion, a P/E ratio of 13.12, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.52 and a beta of 1.23.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, November 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.91 earnings per share for the quarter, beating analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.78 by $0.13. Apple had a return on equity of 48.68% and a net margin of 22.41%. The business had revenue of $62.90 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $61.55 billion. During the same quarter in the prior year, the business earned $2.07 EPS. The firm’s revenue for the quarter was up 19.6% on a year-over-year basis. As a group, equities analysts expect that Apple Inc. will post 11.88 earnings per share for the current year.
AAPL has been the subject of a number of recent research reports. JPMorgan Chase & Co. reaffirmed a “buy” rating and set a $272.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday, October 10th. Rosenblatt Securities set a $200.00 price target on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Monday, October 22nd. Bank of America reaffirmed a “buy” rating on shares of Apple in a research report on Tuesday, October 9th. UBS Group set a $250.00 price target on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Monday, October 8th. Finally, Citigroup upped their price target on Apple from $230.00 to $265.00 and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Monday, October 8th. Three investment analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-four have issued a hold rating and twenty-two have given a buy rating to the company. Apple has an average rating of “Hold” and a consensus target price of $195.33.
In related news, insider Chris Kondo sold 3,408 shares of the stock in a transaction on Monday, November 19th. The stock was sold at an average price of $190.00, for a total value of $647,520.00. Following the sale, the insider now owns 8,940 shares in the company, valued at approximately $1,698,600. About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers. It also sells various related software, services, accessories, and third-party digital content and applications. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and Mac, a line of desktop and portable personal computers, as well as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems.
